newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia foreign minister says ASEAN bid on track.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia foreign minister says ASEAN bid on track.

text.p: Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot said on Thursday he did not expect recent political troubles to prevent his country from joining the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) this year.
"As far as Cambodia is concerned, there is no question about it," he said when asked about ASEAN, which Cambodia hopes to join in July along with fellow observer nations Burma and Laos.
Two ASEAN diplomats, who asked not to be identified, said they were confident Cambodia would gain ASEAN entry this year despite internal problems.

Ung Huot said he had decided on a list of Cambodia delegates for ASEAN's July meeting in anticipation of entry into the regional club, which groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Ung Huot was speaking to reporters after signing an agreement with China on technical cooperation on health.

At least two problems have raised concerns about Cambodia's entry into ASEAN: recent political tensions between co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen and a lack of progress in passing legislation required for membership.

The troubled Ranariddh-Hun Sen coalition, formed after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, has dropped to an all-time low in recent weeks after a deadly grenade attack on an opposition rally and a split within Ranariddh's party.
Ranariddh has accused Hun Sen of masterminding the split in a "coup d'etat".
Ung Huot acknowledged the coalition goverment was troubled and that foreign embassies had stepped up security in recent days, but said "the worst is over. It can only get better".

As for technical requirements for joining ASEAN, Ung Huot said the ASEAN secretariat was pleased with Cambodia's progress and noted that on Wednesday the Council of Ministers approved 19 economic and diplomatic measures needed for membership.
But those measures must now be approved by the National Assembly, which has failed to convene after a long break because of political instability.
